roleplay.heading: Opus 5 acted out a harness
roleplay.body: In 6 of its 15 attempts, Opus 5 didn't answer the brief. It wrote out tool calls and their results as if it were an agent with a terminal, which it wasn't: Rig 0 gives the model no tools. Every command and every result below is invented. Twice the fake 'file' had HTML inside it; the other four times there was nothing to play.
roleplay.source: From the 16-bit fighter sprite, attempt #1. The reply's first 22 lines, unedited apart from one redaction.

footnote.heading: Footnote: the film Opus 5 hid
footnote.body: Opus 5's first micro-film attempt came back as a fake 'write file' tool call, with a complete HTML film inside it as an escaped string. What it delivered was the tool call, so the verdict stands: fail, 3rd. Below is the film it hid, decoded mechanically, byte for byte, with no edits. It was never re-judged.

method.intro: Rig 0 is the bare setup every Drop runs on.
points: One headless call per brief, with no tools, no files, no memory and no conversation. The system prompt is one neutral line.
Three attempts per model per brief. Attempt #1 is the headline and was fixed before anyone looked.

Blind judging: each attempt #1 shown as A, B or C, judged pass or fail against one fixed bar with a sentence of why, then ranked. The key was committed before any verdict. Then the key opened and attempts #2 and #3 were read for consistency. No scores and no averages.
Effort was set to high for every model. At max, a throwaway bouncing-ball brief took 57 minutes and 345,000 thinking tokens, against 1.6 minutes at high.
The command-line tool stepped in once: before Opus 5's first flour-sack reply, it sent one automatic message. That take is flagged where it appears.
Column position: the random shuffle put Opus 5.5 in column A on 4 of the 5 briefs. Later Drops balance column positions.
What Rig 0 still tells the model: the working folder, the account's email address, and a one-line preamble saying it is a Claude agent. That preamble is the likely trigger for Opus 5's role-play.
method.fingerprint_line: Each brief is sealed. Its SHA-256 is taken over the exact message sent to the model, and every Drop shows these same fingerprints. A brief's text is published when it retires, so anyone can check it.
